$comment: EVERY PUBLIC FACTUAL CLAIM ON THE SITE, IN ONE FILE.
The whole direction is staked on the visitor believing what they are shown.
That only survives contact with a deadline if it is enforced by the build
rather than by memory, so nothing may state a fact about the real world
verified:false is a DEVELOPMENT PLACEHOLDER. The UI marks it visibly, and
`node scripts/check-content.mjs --production` fails the build while any
launch-blocking claim is still unverified. Do not flip `verified` to true
without putting the evidence in `source` and the measurement date in `asOf`.
The checklist for gathering these is docs/redesign-2026/CONTENT-REQUIRED.md,
and it is generated from this file so the two cannot drift.

claims.label: Total machines under management
claims.location: Hero horizon, hero gauges, fleet section
claims.why: The horizon draws one peg per machine. The number IS the picture.
claims.fallback: Drop the exact count. Draw the horizon from branch structure only and remove the N/M gauge.

claims.label: Machines currently reporting online
claims.why: The seven grey pegs are the most credible thing on the page. A marketing site shows 97/97.
claims.fallback: Remove the online split and show machines only. The pegs then carry branch state, not uptime.

claims.label: Number of branches
claims.why: The spine breaks into one segment per branch. Structure, not decoration.
claims.fallback: Draw a single unbroken spine and drop the branch labels.

claims.label: The nine branch names
claims.why: Named under each spine segment. Cities were chosen deliberately over client venues: naming a segment after Roshn or Boulevard would assert a deployment we cannot evidence.
claims.fallback: Label segments by index (١–٩) with no place names.

claims.label: Which specific machines are offline, and per-machine revenue
claims.why: Drives the per-peg readout. Never published as a headline figure.
claims.fallback: Already safe: the readout is labelled as illustrative and shows no branch-identifying data.

claims.label: Total purchases (currency), single month
claims.source: R.Pay operator dashboard, TOTAL PURCHASES tile, 01-31 May 2025. Shown with a riyal symbol alongside TOTAL REVERSALS 32,567.85 SAR and TOTAL PROFIT 162,839.25 SAR. Count tiles on the same dashboard (97 machines, 9 branches, 2 users) carry no currency symbol.
claims.why: Previously carried as a transaction COUNT and rendered as "465,255 عملية مكتملة". It is a currency total, not a count, so that label overstated activity by an unknown multiple. The dashboard it came from covers one month on an account with 2 users, which reads as demo or pilot data of unverified provenance rather than lifetime platform volume.
claims.fallback: Render no figure and no counter. The stat row shows the two remaining tiles and an em dash in this slot; the section still reads because the machines figure and the client logos carry the scale.

claims.label: Prizes and gifts delivered
claims.source: Carried from R.Pay's own production site
claims.why: The most human number the company owns.
claims.fallback: Omit the line entirely.

claims.label: Amount settled today
claims.why: A live-feeling figure. Also the most commercially sensitive number on the page.
claims.fallback: Already applied: the gauge is omitted rather than filled with a plausible number. Decide whether it may be published at all.

claims.label: Accepted payment methods
claims.source: Carried from R.Pay's own production site
claims.why: Answers the first question every operator has.
claims.fallback: Show only the methods that can be evidenced. The row degrades cleanly to any subset.

claims.label: Customer and venue marks
claims.why: Third-party trademarks. Displaying them without written permission is a legal exposure, not a design decision.
claims.fallback: SHIPPED BY DEFAULT: the section is built as a typographic register that carries deployment CLASS and city, and works with zero logos. Marks are additive, never structural.

claims.label: Named customer deployments
claims.why: A named venue is a claim about somebody else's business.
claims.fallback: Unnamed deployment classes only: arcade, vending, coffee, with city omitted.

claims.label: Product name for the terminal
claims.why: Naming the hardware turns a service company into one that makes a thing. Needs owner approval and KSA/GCC trademark clearance, classes 9 and 36.
claims.fallback: Refer to it as 'the terminal' throughout. Costs nothing structurally.

claims.label: Terminal specifications
claims.why: Publishing an IP rating or EMV level that cannot be evidenced is a legal exposure. NOTHING is currently published.
claims.fallback: Already applied: no specification is stated anywhere. The section describes behaviour, not certification.

claims.label: Is R.Pay the region's largest arcade operator, or does it serve them?
claims.why: Earlier concepts contradict each other. These are opposite companies: if R.Pay IS the operator, every competing operator is being asked to fund a competitor.
claims.fallback: Already applied: the site claims neither. Copy describes what the system does, never who is largest.

claims.label: Official Arabic entity name
claims.source: rpay.sa footer, retrieved 2026-08-19: «جميع الحقوق محفوظة © 2026 شركة آر باي السعودية.» — the same line, with the same hamza-alif spelling of آر باي, is what the site publishes about itself.
claims.why: The name the company puts its own copyright behind. Split out of company.registration so the registration numbers keep blocking on their own.
claims.fallback: n/a — resolved.

claims.label: CR number, VAT number, registered address
claims.why: Legally required on a Saudi commercial site, and the cheapest trust signal available. The entity NAME is resolved separately — see company.legalName; these three are not.
claims.fallback: Footer renders without the registration block. It is built to omit, not to show blanks.

claims.label: What is behind the control-room tour CTA
claims.why: The page names a concrete 15-minute offer. Who runs it, on which days, with what response time.
claims.fallback: CTA becomes a WhatsApp conversation rather than a booked walkthrough. One string change.

claims.label: WhatsApp number, sales phone, sales email, lead destination
claims.why: The conversion path has to land somewhere real.
claims.fallback: CTAs are inert in development and visibly marked as such.

claims.label: What R.Pay offers a venue that HOSTS machines
claims.why: The second audience. Revenue share, footfall data, installation and maintenance terms. This content exists nowhere in the current site.
claims.fallback: Already applied: the section states only what the system verifiably does for a host and asks them to talk, rather than inventing commercial terms.

claims.label: Privacy policy and PDPL position
claims.why: The contact form captures personal data under Saudi PDPL.
claims.fallback: The form is disabled until a policy exists. It does not collect anything in development.
